object_description: large platform building with circulation externalised as peripheral passageways around a dense core
geometry_property: thick service walls at the core
design_condition: the building is located and oriented from north to south so that it works both as an autonomous object today and as part of the future densification of the campus along the strengthening main axis

positive: The location is part of the visual and landscape continuities specific to the current campus
It anticipates the evolution of the main axis as a structuring element strengthening over time
It also anticipates a network of constructions that could later restructure the site
The project is designed both as an autonomous object and to fit future densification
The proposed spatiality is flexible and scalable in continuity with the territorial reflections
Large platforms externalise the major horizontal and vertical circulations
Technical flows and service circulations are concentrated in thick walls at the core
The spatial signature lies in placing outside what is usually in the centre
The peripheral passageway reinterprets the sun breakers of the first campus buildings
The system seeks a working environment favouring exchange and stimulation
Double-height spaces for informal meetings and autonomous appropriation form a manifesto
The project affirms that learning and research are primarily collective and collaborative activities
The jury salutes a form of research developed from the specificities of the academic teaching space
The project speaks of memory and becoming, of sedimented territories and future spatial practices
The typology distinguishes three types of flows allowing great programmatic flexibility
The peripheral passageways are ideally lit and naturally ventilated
Natural ventilation may be enough to control the summer climate in the passageways
The cost of exterior fittings is in the lower range and floor areas are average
negative: Locations of premises are questionable, in particular the proximity of research and practical work spaces
The transparency and visibility of laboratories will need to be clarified and modulated
A significant deficit in technical premises and storage is noted
The principle of access for deliveries must be clarified
Practical work rooms over different levels pose logistical problems and need more supervision
The glass skin mechanised by hydraulic cylinders is not desired for operation, maintenance and safety
The penetration of light towards the study and research areas raises questions
Winter appropriation of the passageways will depend on their temperature
The spans are too large and optimisations are possible without harming the concept
The cost of the work falls within the upper range due to the estimated cost of the passageways
The implementation and extension stages will need to be refined
